title: Lifecycle, Signals, and Incident Recovery
readerIntent: Operate startup, readiness, drain, shutdown, governed change, and incidents.
priorKnowledge: Know the deployment topology and owned resources.
owner: Single lifecycle coordinator, module contributors, diagnostics, and nDynamo
summary: The process moves through starting, started, degraded, draining, stopping, stopped, or failed; bounded contributors report readiness and release resources in deterministic order.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
items: Required startup dependencies affect readiness; optional control-plane integrations recover asynchronously.
Liveness proves the process exists; readiness admits traffic only while started.
SIGTERM/SIGINT transitions to draining, rejects new work, waits boundedly, then closes resources.
Hard OOM/SIGKILL cannot run hooks; external supervision, replicas, durable ownership, and reconciliation are mandatory.

sections.heading: Governed runtime change
items: Preview is side-effect free and reports changes, impact, warnings, and destructive risk.
Approval records immutable intent and separation of duties.
Activation validates digest, revision, tenant, actor, and policy before using the owning service.
Audit correlates success/failure; rollback restores the prior snapshot through the same authority.
Secrets and prototype-mutating paths are rejected.

sections.heading: Incident flow
items: Correlate health, readiness, traces, safe logs/metrics, audit, provider state, queues, jobs, carriers, publications, and recent activations.
Contain traffic or work, preserve evidence, recover owned state, reconcile derived systems, and verify business outcome.
Never use sensitive values as telemetry labels or expose protected readiness details as public probes.
